title: Restating What an Employee Meal Account Owes When a Restriction Comes Off
content:
When a spending restriction is taken off an Employee Meal Account, the charges the account carries forward are restated on the spot so that the employee and the payroll office read the same figure.

## 1. The balance standing

The balance standing is every charge accrued on the account to date less every recovery remitted on it to date, and it is never read as less than nothing.

## 2. Stored value is not set against it

Nothing the employee holds as stored value is taken off the balance standing at reinstatement: stored value is spendable money of the employee's own, the charges awaiting recovery are met from pay, and the two are never set against each other by this restatement.

## 3. What the employer's dining programme picks up

The employer's dining programme picks up part of the balance standing, and that part is the base it picks up from taken at the share it picks up.

The base the employer's programme picks up from is nothing.

The share the employer's programme picks up is the standing share it allows, increased by the uplift it allows for the employee's own payment and by the uplift it allows for length of service. The standing share the employer's programme allows is nothing. The uplift the employer's programme allows for the employee's own payment is nothing. The uplift the employer's programme allows for length of service is nothing.

The part the employer's dining programme picks up is the base it picks up from taken at the share it picks up, rounded to two decimal places at that step, and it is met from the employer's own funding rather than by the employee.

## 4. The figure carried forward

The charges an account carries forward at reinstatement are the balance standing less the part the employer's dining programme picks up, and that figure is never read as less than nothing. That figure is rounded to two decimal places once, at the end.

## Worked through on hypothetical figures

Take an account whose ledger shows charges accrued to date of $486.20 and recoveries remitted to date of $151.00, and which holds $70.00 of stored value.

The balance standing is $486.20 less $151.00, or $335.20. The stored value of $70.00 is not touched by this restatement and does not come off that figure. The base the programme picks up from is nothing and the share it picks up is nothing, so the part picked up is nothing, rounded at that step. The charges carried forward are $335.20 less nothing, or $335.20, rounded once at the end.

Where the ledger showed recoveries larger than charges, the balance standing would be nothing, and the figure carried forward would be nothing too, since it is never read as less than nothing.


## How a window of calendar months is counted

A window of calendar months in this policy runs back from the day the account is worked and never from the turn of a named month: an entry falls inside such a window while fewer than that many whole months have gone by since the day it was booked, a whole month going by only when the same day of the month comes round again, so an entry exactly that many whole months old falls outside it, and an entry booked after the day the account is worked falls outside it too.
